THORACIC ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/13/2025
Stage IIIA NSCLC, RUL, s/p concurrent chemoradiation (carboplatin/paclitaxel weekly + 60 Gy) completed 12/13/2024.
Post-treatment CT 01/08: RUL mass 2.3 cm, nodes decreased, no new disease.
Fatigue improving. Cough unchanged. Eating better.
Plan: start durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks today, for 12 months. Discussed immune side effects - cough or breathlessness (pneumonitis), diarrhea, rash, thyroid changes - and to call for any of them. Surveillance CT every 3 months.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Office Visit - after chemoradiation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Finished chemo/radiation 12/13. Tired, naps most afternoons, improving week by week. First durvalumab dose 1/13, no issues so far. Cough about the same, no blood. Eating more. Breathing at baseline, albuterol a few times a week. Still sneaking 3-4 cigarettes a day - embarrassed about it.
O: Weight 74 kg (about 78 in October). Vitals otherwise as charted. Lungs: no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P
1. NSCLC IIIA, good response on CT 1/8 (2.3 cm). On durvalumab q4 weeks via oncology. Reviewed which symptoms should prompt a call to them (new cough or shortness of breath, diarrhea, rash).
2. Tobacco: a few a day. No judgment; offered patch again - wants to keep tapering on his own.
3. COPD: stable.
4. Fatigue: expected after treatment; oncology following counts.
RTC spring.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD - received 09/19/2025
Date of visit: 09/14/2025

HPI: 48M with COPD and stage III non-small cell lung cancer on durvalumab, here with two days of increasing breathlessness and cough productive of green sputum.
Meds: tiotropium, albuterol inhalers; durvalumab every 4 weeks (oncology).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father COPD; paternal uncle lung cancer.
Social: smoker, 30 pack-years.

Triage: RR 22, SpO2 88% on room air.
Exam: tachypneic, diffuse expiratory wheezes throughout.
ABG: pH 7.32, PaCO2 55, PaO2 70.
CXR: bronchial wall thickening, no consolidation.

Impression: acute exacerbation of COPD with acute respiratory acidosis.
ED course: continuous nebulized albuterol/ipratropium, steroids and antibiotics started, BiPAP initiated.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - received 09/19/2025
Admitted 09/14/2025, discharged 09/17/2025.
Principal diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD.
Other: stage IIIA NSCLC on consolidation durvalumab; tobacco use.

Course: admitted from the ED with hypercapnic exacerbation. Noninvasive ventilation overnight on admission, then nasal cannula; back on room air by the second hospital day. Treated with scheduled nebulized albuterol/ipratropium, prednisone 40 mg daily (5-day course) and azithromycin (5-day course). Chest imaging without consolidation; the team did not find evidence of pneumonitis. Oncology aware.

Discharge medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily; albuterol HFA as needed; prednisone 40 mg daily to complete 5 days (last dose 09/18); azithromycin to complete 5 days (last dose 09/18).
Allergies: none known.
Follow-up: primary care in 1-2 weeks; oncology as scheduled. Smoking cessation advised.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after hospital discharge 9/17 for COPD flare. Finished prednisone and azithromycin 9/18. Breathing much better, back to his usual rescue use. No fever. Using tiotropium daily. Offered a follow-up visit this week or next - he'd rather wait, sees oncology on the 13th and says he's 'had enough appointments.' Advised to call or text for any worsening. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: RE: Post-discharge call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks - read the discharge summary. Ok to hold off; front desk please offer him an October slot for a check plus flu shot.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD - received 04/06/2026
Date of visit: 03/28/2026

HPI: 49M with COPD, tobacco use and stage IIIA NSCLC treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab (completed 12/2025), brought in by his sister. Over the past week he has become more confused and sluggish and has hardly been eating. She says he has dropped close to 7 kg in two months and has had an ongoing cough with occasional streaks of blood.
Meds: tiotropium, albuterol.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father COPD; paternal uncle lung cancer.
Social: 30 pack-year smoker.

Vitals: BP 116/74, HR 84.
Exam: drowsy, oriented to name only. Moist mucous membranes. No peripheral edema. Lungs without crackles. No focal motor deficit.
Labs: Na 117, serum osm 247, urine osm 486, urine Na 58, K 3.9, creatinine 0.7, glucose 104, TSH 1.9. Hgb 12.6.
CT head: no acute abnormality.
CT chest: central RUL mass 5.8 cm, larger than in October, with enlarged mediastinal nodes.

Impression: severe hypotonic hyponatremia from SIADH, in the setting of progressive lung cancer. Euvolemic.
Plan: fluid restriction, admit to medicine with frequent sodium checks.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - received 04/06/2026
Admitted 03/28/2026, discharged 04/02/2026.
Principal diagnosis: hyponatremia due to SIADH.
Secondary: progression of stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe; COPD; tobacco use.

Course: presented confused with Na 117, low serum osmolality, concentrated urine and high urine sodium while clinically euvolemic; TSH 1.9 and AM cortisol 17, both normal. Managed with fluid restriction to 1 L/day and sodium chloride 1 g tablets three times daily, correcting slowly. Sodium 128 on day of discharge; mentation back to his baseline by day 3. Blood-streaked sputum only, hemoglobin stable at 12.6. CT chest showed growth of the central RUL mass to 5.8 cm with enlarged mediastinal nodes. Oncology consulted: progression after chemoradiation and durvalumab; plan second-line systemic therapy as an outpatient.

Discharge medications: tiotropium 18 mcg daily; albuterol HFA as needed; sodium chloride 1 g by mouth three times daily. Fluid restriction 1 L/day.
Allergies: none known.
Follow-up: oncology next week with BMP; primary care.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Records filed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospital records received and reviewed: SIADH with Na 117, progression of the RUL cancer. Discharged on fluid restriction and salt tabs, oncology starting second-line treatment. Asked front desk to reach out to him about coming in.

documents.title: Hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I was in the hospital last week, my sodium was really low and I was out of it. Cancer grew back. Starting new chemo next week with oncology. I'm ok, my sister is staying with me for a bit. Is it ok to keep using my inhalers the same?

documents.title: RE: Hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, thank you for telling me - I read the hospital records and I'm sorry this came back. Yes, keep both inhalers exactly as before. Stick with the 1 liter fluid limit and the salt tablets until oncology changes them, and get your blood checks with them. I'd like to see you once treatment is underway - the front desk will reach out, or text me a time that works.

Plan: second-line docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV every 21 days, cycle 1 today. Continue fluid restriction and salt tablets; BMP with each cycle. Restage after 4 cycles.
